instrument_note: 4-scenario rotation (1 per dimension from pool of 3)

labels: She is abandoning people who depended on her
She earned the opportunity and her team will adapt
She should have made sure her team was taken care of before leaving
Other
judgment.other_text: Her choices do have consequences, but scrutinizing her is ridiculous when the corporate system is designed to neglect or abuse all parties involved. The system worked as designed.

labels: When you build something with people, you owe them loyalty
Professional growth is a legitimate priority — teams are not permanent
A good leader ensures continuity before moving on
Other
reasoning.other_text: If a corporate system is designed to produce continuity, it will. If it isn't, it won't.

labels: Those closest to the organization should receive help first
Those in greatest need should receive help first
Everyone affected deserves equal consideration regardless of connection
Other
judgment.other_text: Established, time-tested principles for resource rationing from trustworthy institutions should be followed.

labels: You owe the most to those you know and have relationships with
Severity of need is the only morally relevant criterion
Fairness requires equal treatment regardless of relationship
The community’s long-term survival depends on protecting the most vulnerable
Other
reasoning.other_text: We must minimize loss of life first and then minimize suffering.

labels: The restaurant should respect the neighborhood’s established customs
A business can serve whatever it chooses — customers will decide with their wallets
The residents’ concerns are worth hearing, but a business has no obligation to conform
Other
judgment.other_text: Neither side is morally right or wrong for the experience they are having.

labels: Neighborhoods have a character worth preserving and newcomers should respect it
In a free society, businesses operate by market rules, not community approval
Dialogue between the restaurant and residents is more productive than moral judgment
Other
reasoning.other_text: There are many different ways of being co-existing on planet Earth. They're bound to bump into each other from time to time.

labels: She did the right thing by fixing what she knew was wrong
She should have followed her manager’s instruction and waited
Her intent was good but going around her manager creates other problems
Other
judgment.other_text: "Quietly" correcting the errors isn't high-integrity, but the change needing leadership review suggests an inappropriately controlling authority-based power structure.

labels: Accuracy matters more than following a chain of command
Organizations depend on people respecting established processes
She should have escalated rather than acted alone
A manager’s instructions should be followed unless clearly unethical
Other
reasoning.other_text: Accuracy matters in proportion to the consequences of innacuracy. You should do what you say you will do (no deception). Decisions should be devolved down to the people at the point of action, while also ensuring they see how their choices affect others.
